blocks.text: Software Tester — Diploma in Computer Engineering / Information Technology

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Engineering, Technology & Computing
EDUCATION PATHWAY
Diploma in Computer Engineering / IT
Typically a 3-year diploma after Class 10, depending on the entry route and institution.
CAREER AREA
Software Quality Assurance (QA)
Manual testing, automation testing, API testing, defect tracking and software quality improvement.

A Software Tester checks whether a software application works as expected, identifies defects and helps development teams deliver reliable products. Testers validate functionality, usability, compatibility, performance and security-related behaviour within their assigned scope.
Software testing is suitable for diploma graduates who enjoy problem-solving, logical thinking, attention to detail and understanding how applications behave under different conditions.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Analyse requirements and identify test scenarios.
Prepare test cases and test data.
Perform manual testing on websites, mobile applications and software systems.
Report bugs with clear reproduction steps and evidence.
Retest fixes and perform regression testing.
Test APIs and database operations where required.
Use automation tools to execute repeatable tests.
Collaborate with developers, product teams and QA engineers.
Maintain test reports and communicate release risks.

blocks.label: Common workplaces
blocks.text: IT service companies, software product firms, startups, fintech companies, e-commerce businesses, healthcare technology companies and internal software teams.
Stage 1 — Class 10
Build foundations in mathematics, logical reasoning, computer basics and written communication.
Stage 2 — Diploma in Computer Engineering / IT
Learn programming, databases, operating systems, networking, web technologies, software engineering and basic data structures.
Stage 3 — Testing practice and projects
Build test cases, practise bug reporting, test APIs and learn an automation framework through sample projects.
Stage 4 — Entry-level employment
Target QA Trainee, Software Tester, Manual Tester, Junior QA Engineer or Automation Tester Trainee roles based on demonstrated skills.
Year 1 — Programming and computer fundamentals
Focus on the technical foundations needed to understand software behaviour.

blocks.label: Learn one programming language
blocks.text: Java or Python.

items.text: Study variables, data types, conditions, loops, functions and basic object-oriented programming.
Understand HTML, CSS and basic JavaScript.
Learn database fundamentals and SQL queries.
Study operating systems, computer networks and software development basics.
Practise logical reasoning and structured problem-solving.
Learn how to use a browser's developer tools.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Create a simple web form and test its validation.
Write basic SQL queries to retrieve and filter records.
Document expected versus actual results for a small application.
Prepare a checklist for testing a login page.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Manual testing and software quality
Focus on the testing process and how to identify defects systematically.

items.text: Understand the software development life cycle (SDLC) and software testing life cycle (STLC).
Learn functional, non-functional, smoke, sanity, exploratory and regression testing.
Practise equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis.
Write clear test scenarios and test cases.
Learn defect life-cycle terminology, severity and priority.
Understand browser compatibility, responsive design and usability testing.
Learn Agile, Scrum, sprint workflows and test documentation.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Test a registration and login workflow.
Create a test plan for an e-commerce checkout.
Report defects with steps to reproduce, expected results and actual results.
Execute regression testing after a sample application update.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Automation, APIs and job readiness
Focus on building practical testing projects and selecting a specialisation.

items.text: Learn Selenium with Java or Playwright with JavaScript/TypeScript.
Practise API testing using Postman.
Learn HTTP methods, status codes, headers, authentication and JSON.
Use SQL to validate data stored by an application.
Learn Git and GitHub for version control.
Understand basic CI/CD concepts and how automated tests run in a pipeline.
Build a structured test suite and publish suitable sample work.
Complete an internship or supervised project where available.

blocks.text: Final-year project ideas

items.text: Automated regression suite for an e-commerce demo application.
API test collection for a sample REST service.
Test management and defect-tracking dashboard.
Cross-browser test suite for a responsive website.
Automated validation of a registration and login workflow.

rows.text: Testing fundamentals
Test scenarios, test cases, test plans and test execution
Manual testing
Functional, regression, smoke, exploratory and usability testing
Test design
Boundary-value analysis, equivalence partitioning and decision tables
Bug reporting
Reproduction steps, evidence, severity, priority and retesting
Programming
Java or Python; basic object-oriented programming
Web technologies
HTML, CSS, JavaScript and browser developer tools
SQL
SELECT, filtering, joins, aggregates and data validation
API testing
HTTP methods, status codes, JSON, authentication and assertions
Automation
Selenium or Playwright, assertions, test fixtures and reusable test code
Collaboration
Git, Agile workflows, documentation and clear communication

blocks.text: Test management and defect tracking
Jira for issue tracking; TestRail or similar tools for test-case management where available. Start with a spreadsheet if you are learning independently.
Automation frameworks
Selenium with Java or Python, or Playwright with JavaScript/TypeScript. Master one framework before learning several.
API testing
Postman for API requests, assertions, collections and environment variables; later, explore automated API testing in code.
Database and version control
MySQL or PostgreSQL for SQL practice; Git and GitHub for version control and portfolio projects.
Performance testing
JMeter or k6 for introductory load-testing exercises. Learn safe, authorised testing practices before testing real systems.
Manual Software Tester
Tests application workflows manually, creates test cases, identifies defects and validates fixes.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: beginners who enjoy observation, structured thinking and investigating unexpected behaviour.
Automation Test Engineer
Develops automated tests, maintains test frameworks and integrates repeatable checks into software delivery workflows.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who enjoy programming, debugging and improving repetitive processes.
API Test Engineer
Validates backend endpoints, response codes, data formats, authentication and error handling.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students interested in backend systems, HTTP, databases and integration testing.
Performance Test Engineer
Evaluates response time, throughput, resource usage and application behaviour under simulated workloads.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who enjoy data analysis, systems behaviour and troubleshooting bottlenecks.
Consider these options based on your target role.

items.text: ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL): a recognised testing-fundamentals certification; review the current syllabus and exam requirements.

blocks.label: Java or Python programming
blocks.text: strengthen the language used by your chosen automation framework.

blocks.label: Selenium or Playwright
blocks.text: develop practical browser-automation skills through projects.

blocks.label: Postman API testing
blocks.text: practise API collections, assertions and environment management.

blocks.label: SQL fundamentals
blocks.text: learn to verify application data and investigate database-related defects.

blocks.label: Git and CI/CD basics
blocks.text: understand source control and automated test execution.

blocks.label: Performance testing
blocks.text: introductory training with JMeter or k6 for load and response-time testing.
Certificates can support a job application, but practical projects and the ability to explain testing decisions are equally important.
Look for internships or project opportunities with:

items.text: Software development companies and IT service providers.
SaaS and software product startups.
Fintech, e-commerce and healthcare technology teams.
Mobile and web application development companies.
QA consulting and software testing service providers.
College projects or open-source projects with accessible testing tasks.

blocks.text: During an internship, aim to learn:

items.text: How requirements become test scenarios.
How test cases are written, executed and updated.
How to report and prioritise defects.
How developers and testers collaborate during a sprint.
How API and database checks support functional testing.
How automation tests are maintained when applications change.

rows.text: Entry level
QA Trainee, Manual Tester, Software Tester
Early career
QA Engineer, Software Test Engineer, Junior Automation Tester
With demonstrated competence
Automation Test Engineer, API Test Engineer, Senior QA Engineer
Advanced technical roles
SDET, Performance Test Engineer, QA Automation Specialist
Longer-term progression
QA Lead, Test Manager, Quality Engineering Manager

blocks.text: Progression depends on demonstrated skills, experience, project exposure and employer requirements. An SDET role generally requires stronger programming and software engineering skills than a manual-testing role.
Examples of employers and industry groups worth researching include:

items.text: IT services companies such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Cognizant.
Software product and cloud companies.
Fintech, banking technology, e-commerce and healthcare software organisations.
QA consulting firms and software testing service providers.
Early-stage startups that build web, mobile or enterprise applications.

blocks.text: These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current vacancies. Search official career pages and internship portals for QA trainee, software tester and junior automation roles. Check each job description for diploma eligibility because some employers require a bachelor's degree.
Suggested portfolio contents

items.text: A test plan and test cases for a sample web application.
A clear defect report with reproduction steps and expected versus actual results.
A Postman collection with API assertions.
SQL queries used to validate sample application data.
An automation project using Selenium or Playwright.
A README explaining setup, test coverage and how to run the tests.
A sample test execution report and internship documentation, if available.

blocks.text: Use demo applications, your own projects or systems for which you have permission to test. Do not test real websites or APIs without authorisation.
Software testing is evolving toward continuous testing, automation and quality engineering. Useful directions include:

items.text: AI-assisted test generation and test maintenance.
API and microservices testing.
Continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD).
Cloud-based cross-browser testing.
Performance and reliability testing.
Accessibility and usability testing.
Security testing fundamentals within authorised environments.
Quality engineering and software development in test (SDET).

blocks.label: Recommended strategy
blocks.text: Learn manual testing fundamentals first, then add SQL and API testing. Build automation skills with one programming language and one framework to become more competitive for technical QA roles.
Tick off each milestone as it is completed.
Employability milestones
0 of 10
Understand SDLC, STLC and core testing concepts.
Write clear test cases for a sample application.
Practise functional, regression and exploratory testing.
Create detailed bug reports with reproduction steps.
Learn SQL queries for data validation.
Test APIs using Postman.
Learn Java or Python fundamentals.

Publish two or more documented testing projects.

Reset checklist
By the end of the diploma and practical training, a job-ready candidate should be able to:

items.text: Understand software development and testing workflows.
Create test cases from requirements and execute them systematically.
Identify, document and retest software defects.
Use SQL and API tools to validate application behaviour.
Write basic automated tests using a chosen framework.
Collaborate with developers and communicate issues clearly.
Demonstrate practical testing skills through a portfolio.

blocks.label: Best starting point
blocks.text: Master manual testing, SQL and API testing before specialising in automation. Build two or three complete projects and verify that each target employer accepts diploma graduates for its entry-level QA roles.
